source.reason: The overall 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C microstructure is defined by the discontinuous precipitation of austenite into γ + κ lamellae, supported by hardness tables and EDS.

overall_structure.value: Discontinuous (and precipitation) transformation of austenite: the microstructure is a banded, rolling-direction-aligned structure in which almost all of the austenite volume transformed into γ + κ-carbide fine lamellar colonies (discontinuous precipitation), with only a few band-shaped γ austenite regions surviving; some δ-phase may also be present. The non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite featured nano-sized κ-carbide precipitation. Dark transformed matrix is crossed by many bright white elongated bands/stringers.

source.reason: Phase evolution γ → γ + κ by discontinuous precipitation, with grain-boundary migration, is described in b0034, b0067, b0068 and b0033; EDS Table 3 gives the phase-constituent partition.

phase_evolution.value: γ → γ + κ discontinuous precipitation at 600 °C: a lower driving force caused by the lower annealing temperature (600 °C) allowed grain-boundary migration of the forming lamellar phase rather than completing lamellae separation; intergranular κ-carbides form on γ/γ boundaries. The residual austenite is present as band-shaped regions among the γ + κ lamellae, indicating a non-complete reaction.

interface_notes.value: Interfaces involved are the γ/κ lamellar interphase boundaries produced by discontinuous precipitation and the δ/γ boundaries (δ phase possibly present). EDS (Table 3) partitions Al (δ 7.8–8.7, γ 7.6–8.0, K 8.0–8.3, γ nano-k 7.8–8.1 wt%) and Mn (δ 9.7–10.0, γ 9.9–10.7, k 10.2–10.5, γ nano-k 13.2–13.6 wt%) across δ, γ, κ and nano-κ constituents in this 600 °C tempered alloy.

validation_against_experiment.value: Used qualitatively to explain the thermodynamic gradient in austenite stability between hot-rolling (1150 °C) and tempering (600 °C/800 °C); the γ fraction gradient was detected for 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C and 800 °C, consistent with the observed austenite decompositions.

unmapped_findings: Tempering at 600 °C triggered only slight/incipient transformations (discontinuous precipitation and precipitation transformation) in the 9Al-10Mn-1C alloy, in contrast to 800 °C which triggered complete and widespread transformations (cellular transformation coupled with spinodal decomposition). (b0117)

For 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C the tempering established thermodynamic changes for austenite stability; the manganese (10%) and carbon (1%) concentrations were not high enough to stabilize the γ phase against its own transformation, with the thermal energy introduced at 600 °C and the limited driving force permitting grain-boundary migration of the forming lamellar phase rather than completing lamellae separation. (b0062, b0067, b0068, b0069, b0070, b0071)

Discontinuous precipitation produced γ + κ-carbide fine lamellae in 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C; the best microstructure among the studied alloys is reported to be this 9Al-10Mn-1C at 600 °C, with narrow inter-lamellar spacing, giving the highest hardness value (439 HV) and, per the literature, the better tensile ductility. (b0114, b0118)
The 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C gained outstanding hardness among the alloys featuring 9% aluminium, attributed to the fine γ + κ lamellae with short inter-lamellar spacing. (b0049, b0082, b0108)

EDS on the 600 °C tempered 9Al-10Mn-1C indicated that the non-discontinuous-precipitated austenite contained nano-sized κ-carbide precipitation; the analysis did not give clear and defined results but a reasonable interpretation was given in accordance with the related microscopy observations. (b0034)
